about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2023 only.

rows.table: Town meeting article record with vote tallies
rows.detail: TWO PROMISED TABLES ARE MISSING FROM THE TEXT: the revolving fund spending limits after Article 2 (p162 ends 'for the spending limits as follows:') and the FY24 Capital Plan project list after Article 6 (p163 ends 'as follows:') — the next page begins with the next article in both cases.

rows.table: FY2024 voted operating budget by line number
rows.detail: The extracted table BEGINS mid-list at line 13/Reserve Fund — lines 1 to 12 (debt service, insurance, retirement, workers comp and similar) did not come through OCR and are effectively missing from the text layer.

rows.table: Town and school employee gross wages
rows.detail: The wages themselves are almost entirely absent from the extraction.

rows.table: Capital project funds
rows.detail: The left column mixes an article number and a meeting date in one field ('14 5/15 ATM', '211/20 STM', '6 05/07/22 ATM') and is blank on continuation rows, so rows must be carried down.

The revenue table is not called revenue. It is headed 'FY 2023 RECEIPTS - JUNE 2023' with a 'SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS' recap and a 'GRAND TOTAL' — on page 25, printed sideways, and the table of contents mislabels it 'FY 2022 Receipts' and puts it on the wrong page. That combination is almost certainly why earlier searches concluded this year has no revenue table.
Pages 49-51 are pages 2, 3 and 4 of a nine-page trust fund schedule — the town printed three pages of a longer document into the annual report and the other six pages exist somewhere else entirely.

Pages 190-197 are eight pages of every town and school employee's gross wages, and nothing on those pages says so; only the table of contents identifies them. The text layer has lost almost all of it.

Two tables the warrant articles explicitly promise ('for the spending limits as follows:' after Article 2, and the FY24 Capital Plan 'as follows:' after Article 6) simply are not in the document — the page turns straight to the next article. The Capital Planning Committee report on p108 likewise describes a 12-item, $2,025,010 plan and then does not print it.
The fire department's own call breakdown does not add up: 356 + 1193 + 366 + 18 = 1,933 against the 2,033 stated in the sentence above it.
The 'Collection of Taxes' receivables schedule on pages 54-56 is headed JUNE 30, 2023 but carries a sub-heading reading 'FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES' on all three pages.

The Board of Assessors report (p45-46) contains no valuation or tax rate table at all — just a narrative about 440 abatement applications against 14 the prior year, a 100% turnover of the board, and a delayed five-year revaluation. The only tax rate in the whole report is the single line 'FY'23 TAX RATE- $14.62' on the profile page.

The report carries the regional dispatch district's full statistics for eight other communities (Berlin, Bolton, Boxborough, Devens, DoD, Harvard, Lancaster, Townsend), five years deep — data about other towns, inside Lunenburg's annual report.
Monty Tech reports its FY23 grants as $2,963,607 in the figure block and $3,552,996 in the prose on the same page.

rows.table: Receivables and collection of taxes summary
rows.detail: CAUTION: the OCR renders a sub-heading on all three pages as 'FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES' inside a table headed JUNE 30, 2023 — either a stale template label the town never updated or an OCR misread; check the PDF before quoting.
